title: Compact Function Parameter IDL and Error Semantics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current function/tool calling surface relies on various ad-hoc JSON schema fragments and runtime heuristics. That leads to inconsistent validation behavior between hosted and private deployments, confusing operator error messages, and poor telemetry for automatic repair/coercion flows.

Goal: Define a compact, runtime-friendly parameter IDL (Compact Parameter IDL, CPS) and a typed error semantics for validation and coercion. CPS should be small to author, serializable in function manifests, backwards-compatible with our existing schema adapters, and explicit about coercion policies. Error semantics should support machine-readable codes, actionable messages, and pointers for quick remediation and telemetry.

Scope: CPS v0.2 (initial rollout) covering primitives, enums, arrays, small nested objects (depth <= 3), nullable fields, defaults, and a small set of validation directives (min/max, pattern, allowed). It will not cover full JSON Schema features (no advanced allOf/oneOf/circular refs) in v0.2.

Design constraints: compact syntax (human readable), deterministic coercion rules, stable error codes, opt-in strictness modes, and a clear migration path from legacy JSON Schema fragments.
acceptance_criteria: CPS schema can be embedded in function manifests in the API and SDKs and parsed by runtime without external schema libs
Runtime enforces type constraints and returns typed validation error objects (code + pointer + readable_message) for all validation failures
Coercion policy configurable per-parameter (allow_coerce | reject | repair) with recorded repaired_value and telemetry flag
Backward compatibility adapter translates legacy JSON Schema fragments to CPS where possible; mismatch returns a clear migration error (ERR_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH)
Tests cover examples: missing required fields, enum mismatch, numeric overflow, array element type errors, nested object missing field
Console shows parameter-level cost/latency telemetry when validation or coercion occurs (for rollout analysis)
tasks: Draft CPS grammar and examples (CPS-v0.2 document)
Implement parser in runtime (Go) and lightweight validator in JS SDK
Define validation error taxonomy and telemetry payload (code, input_path, pointer, repaired_value, suggestion)
Add manifest field 'cps_version' and runtime fallback behavior
End-to-end tests and fuzzing for coercion edge cases
Consolidate docs and migration guide for partner teams
discussion: 2026-03-02 meeting: Agreed to adopt a compact IDL instead of full JSON Schema for performance and UX. Key trade-off: limit features to ensure deterministic runtime behavior.
Decision: Use CPS version integer (cps_version: 1) in manifest. Runtime rejects unknown major versions with ERR_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH.
Coercion defaults: strings->numbers allowed only when parameter sets allow_coerce=true. Reject by default for PII-labeled params.
Error object shape: {code, message, input_path, expected, got, repaired_value?, hint?}. We'll surface message and hint to SDKs; repaired_value only when allow_coerce and repair happened.
Design note: For array element errors include element_index in pointer to help UI highlighting. Example pointer: /items[3]/price

PR review feedback (runtime team): keep parser dependency-free to avoid heap allocations at hot path; implement streaming-friendly validation that can short-circuit on first hard error if strict mode enabled.

notes:
CPS core constructs (human-readable):
- type: 'string' | 'int' | 'float' | 'bool' | 'enum' | 'object' | 'array'
- nullable: true|false
- default: literal
- enum: [list]
- items: <type shorthand>
- fields: {k:type, ...} (objects limited depth 3)
- directives: min, max, pattern, allow_coerce, strict_mode

Example CPS snippet:
name: {type:string, pattern:^\w[\w -]{0,62}$, nullable:false}
age: {type:int, min:0, max:130, allow_coerce:true}
items: {type:array, items:{type:object, fields:{id:{type:string}, qty:{type:int}}}}

Validation error codes (initial set):
- ERR_PARAM_MISSING: required param not provided
- ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH: runtime type differs from expected
- ERR_ENUM_MISMATCH: value not in allowed enum set
- ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE: numeric outside min/max
- ERR_PATTERN_MISMATCH: regex failed
- ERR_COERCION_FAILED: attempted coercion couldn't produce valid value
- ERR_SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH: unsupported CPS major version

Error object contract (stringified as JSON in API response):
code: string (one of above)
message: human readable message
input_path: JSON Pointer-like path to value (e.g., /order/items[2]/qty)
expected: short type descriptor
got: short type/value descriptor
repaired_value: present when auto-coercion repaired the input
hint: short remediation suggestion

Telemetry: emit telemetry event on any validation or coercion with flags: was_coerced, code, cps_version, latency_ms. This will power Console heatmaps and regression alerts.
